parsed.summary: Runtime protection gate regressed task/phase selection and does not reliably restore runtime files; tests are failing and an out-of-scope file was modified.
issues: TESTS: make test failed with 6 integration failures, including tests/test_integration.py::test_ralph_phase_mode_marks_final_state_deadlocked_after_last_runnable_task and related task/phase mode regressions.
ACCEPTANCE: not met. The new stash flow logs 'Runtime protection stash was created but could not be resolved', so runtime-owned files are not reliably restored after coder exec.

REGRESSION: resetting tasks.json/progress.md/.ralph/memory before coder exec changes live runtime state used by subsequent task/phase selection, which caused Ralph to report 'Phase R2 complete!' instead of preserving blocked pending tasks.
QUALITY: protection logic depends on resolving the stash later by message lookup, which is brittle and fails in the observed test run.
parsed.fix_instructions: Replace the message-based stash resolution in ralph.sh and src/ralph/resources/ralph.sh with a deterministic capture-and-restore mechanism for tasks.json, progress.md, and .ralph/memory so those files are always restored on both success and failure without altering live task selection state; then remove the unrelated system_promt.md change and rerun the failing integration tests.
parsed.progress_note: R19-01 needs one focused fix: make runtime file protection restoration deterministic and non-regressive.
